title: "BlueEarth Climate Stress Test"
subtitle: "A workflow toolbox for rapid, bottom-up climate risk assessment of water systems"

The **BlueEarth Climate Stress Test (CST)** toolbox helps water resources
specialists examine how river flow responds to changes in climate. It supports
rapid, first-order assessments of water availability, low flows and high flows
in a river basin. The central question is: **under which climate conditions
does a hydrological outcome of concern emerge?**

CST uses a bottom-up, scenario-neutral approach. It starts with the basin's
historical climate, generates alternative weather sequences to represent
natural variability, and applies a systematic range of temperature and
precipitation changes. A distributed Wflow-SBM model simulates the resulting
hydrological response. Indicators calculated from those simulations can be
mapped across the tested climate range as a **response surface**. You can
compare that surface with a decision-relevant threshold to identify conditions
under which performance becomes unacceptable.

CMIP6 projections serve a different purpose. The toolbox summarizes projected
temperature and precipitation changes so you can place the tested range and
any identified vulnerabilities in a plausible future context. Those
projections do not select or drive the stress-test scenarios. This separation
lets an assessment examine climate conditions beyond a chosen model ensemble
and then ask which of those conditions merit closer attention.

This site documents the **workflow toolbox** that performs the analysis. It is
the computational part of the wider CST platform; the API and user interface
are maintained separately. The toolbox uses global datasets and an automated
model setup to make basin-scale screening practical. Results still depend on
the quality of the climate inputs and hydrological model. They are a starting
point for investigating risks and adaptation options, not a substitute for a
locally calibrated model or detailed engineering design.

## The five workflows

The workflows share a project configuration set. The runner executes those you
enable in this order:

1. **Analyze historical climate** (optional) — compare gridded climate sources
   for the basin before choosing the forcing dataset. This analysis does not
   require a hydrological model.
2. **Build the model** — use HydroMT and global datasets to prepare Wflow-SBM,
   then run it with historical forcing and evaluate the simulated discharge
   where observations are available.
3. **Analyze projections** — calculate CMIP6 temperature and precipitation
   change factors by model, scenario and future period for later comparison
   with the stress-test range.
4. **Generate scenarios** — create stochastic weather realizations and apply
   the specified temperature and precipitation perturbations. The resulting
   climate series form a reusable scenario collection.
5. **Simulate the system** — run Wflow-SBM for the generated climate series and
   calculate hydrological indicators from the retained model responses.

Model building and scenario generation are both needed before simulation.
Projection analysis is independent of scenario generation and provides context
for interpreting the response surface. See the [quick start](guide/quick-start.qmd)
for an example run.
